extraction_metadata.notes: Allen Institute for AI (ai2) announcing HiRO-ACEv2, a system for simulating global extreme weather at 3 km resolution at ~1/300th the computational cost of conventional numerical weather prediction. This is the highest-signal climate post of the round — a concrete system with a quantified cost-resolution trade-off, directly relevant to the OSIRIS climate domain (c=0.25 K) and the downscaling discussion.

title: HiRO-ACEv2 simulates global extreme weather at 3 km resolution for ~1/300th the cost
subtitle_or_tagline: AI2's kilometer-scale global weather simulation — extreme events without the supercomputer budget
topic: The Allen Institute for AI announces HiRO-ACEv2, extending their ACE (AI for climate and earth system emulation) line: a learned emulator that simulates global extreme weather at 3 km effective resolution at approximately 1/300th the computational cost of conventional kilometer-scale numerical weather prediction. The system targets extreme events (the tail of the weather distribution — storms, extremes of precipitation and wind) where coarse emulators historically wash out detail, and claims the cost reduction makes kilometer-scale ensemble simulation accessible to research groups and agencies that cannot operate frontier NWP systems.

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Pretrain emulator on historical reanalysis + kilometer-scale NWP archives
Step 2 - Roll out autoregressive global simulation
Step 3 - Resolve extremes at 3 km without explicit convection-parameterization handoff
Step 4 - Run ensembles at 1/300th cost for uncertainty quantification
Step 5 - Distribute to agencies/researchers for extreme-weather decision support

osiris_connection: HiRO-ACEv2 sharpens the OSIRIS climate question from last round: when a learned emulator resolves extremes at 3 km, what bounds its output displacement from the physical truth? The known failure mode of autoregressive weather emulators is roll-out drift — small displacements compounding over horizons until the simulation decorrelates. That compounding is exactly the sum-of-L*c pathology Theorem 7 governs: each emulator step is a Lipschitz operator, and unbounded total drift is the signature of an unclamped rollout. A norm-clamped ACE variant would make the 1/300th-cost claim certifiable — per-step displacement budget c chosen so the ensemble spread remains physically calibrated (the climate domain's c=0.25 K), turning 'cheap kilometer-scale simulation' from an empirical claim into a bounded one.
